nodes.name: Long summer daylight
nodes.desc: Near-constant summer light lets plants and lake algae grow fast in the short warm season.

nodes.name: Volcanic ash soil
nodes.desc: The 1912 Novarupta eruption buried the Valley of Ten Thousand Smokes under deep ash and pumice deposits, where plants are slowly recolonizing.

nodes.name: Cold, short growing season
nodes.desc: Harsh weather and a brief summer shape which plants can grow and when animals can feed.

nodes.name: Salmon-borne nutrients
nodes.desc: Salmon bring ocean-grown nutrients inland, and their remains are broken down into nutrients that feed streamside soil and lakes.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Fungi and bacteria break down salmon carcasses and other dead matter, returning nutrients to soil and water.

nodes.name: Sedges
nodes.desc: Grass-like plants of meadows and coastal flats. Wikipedia lists sedges among the main foods of brown bears.

nodes.name: Black crowberry
nodes.desc: A low evergreen tundra shrub with black berries that birds eat.

nodes.name: Bog bilberry
nodes.desc: A low berry shrub of tundra and bog. Its berries are eaten by bears.

nodes.name: Field horsetail
nodes.desc: A spore-bearing plant that colonizes bare, disturbed ground and is eaten by bears and moose.

nodes.name: White spruce
nodes.desc: A conifer whose seeds feed red squirrels and which forms the forest along park lakes and rivers.

nodes.name: Fireweed
nodes.desc: A tall pink wildflower that quickly colonizes bare or disturbed ground and is browsed by moose.

nodes.name: Phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Microscopic drifting algae that form the base of the food web in park lakes.

nodes.name: Moose
nodes.desc: Browses shrubs, horsetail and other plants. Wikipedia lists moose among park mammals; bears and wolves hunt them.

nodes.name: Arctic ground squirrel
nodes.desc: A burrowing, hibernating rodent of tundra slopes that eats plants and seeds and is prey for bears.

nodes.name: American red squirrel
nodes.desc: Feeds on spruce seeds and is prey for lynx and bears.

nodes.name: Tundra vole
nodes.desc: A small rodent of wet meadows that feeds on sedges and other plants and is eaten by bears.

nodes.name: Zooplankton
nodes.desc: Tiny animals that graze algae in the lakes. Sockeye salmon feed extensively on them.

nodes.name: Sockeye salmon
nodes.desc: Feeds on zooplankton, then returns from the ocean to spawn. Spawning runs into Brooks River bring bears, eagles and gulls to feed.

nodes.name: Canada lynx
nodes.desc: A secretive wild cat listed among park mammals. It hunts squirrels and other small prey.

nodes.name: Glaucous-winged gull
nodes.desc: The most often recorded bird here. Gulls scavenge the remains bears leave from salmon.

nodes.name: Common raven
nodes.desc: An opportunistic omnivore that eats berries and scavenges salmon remains and carrion.

nodes.name: Bald eagle
nodes.desc: Feeds on spawning salmon and on carcasses left on riverbanks.

nodes.name: Brown bear
nodes.desc: Katmai protects one of the largest brown bear populations in the world. Bears eat sedges, berries, and in summer, salmon.

nodes.name: Gray wolf
nodes.desc: Listed among Katmai mammals. Wolves hunt large prey such as moose.
